change.title: stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields

source.quote: Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.

tasks.reasoning:
The repo pins stripe-node 15.12.0, eight majors behind 23.0.0, which pins 2026-09-30.endive. Nothing breaks today because the SDK sends its own older pinned API version. Upgrading means one coherent move through v19 to v23 plus the clover, dahlia and endive API versions. The likely edits are: construct the client with `new Stripe()` everywhere (including the CJS reconcile script); fix type errors from reworked types; re-check subscription and checkout-session fields read from responses, since basil moved current_period_* to items; and align the webhook endpoint API version. The repo uses no payment_method_types, billing_cycle_anchor, constructEventWithoutVerification or v2 APIs. Uncertain: the code scan did not read response handling, so the migration agent must check which subscription and session fields are read.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- stripe:node-22-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 22.0.0: Stripe is a true ES6 class (use new Stripe()), types reworked, per-request host override removed, effective 2026-04-02. Passed through on the way from 15.12.0 to 23.x. Stripe is now a true ES6 class, so any `Stripe(key)` or `require('stripe')(key)` call without `new` must become `new Stripe(key)`. The per-request host override is also gone and the types were reworked, so type errors need fixing in the same PR.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Stripe import is now a true ES6 class. Use `new Stripe()` to create a StripeClient instead of calling it:"
- stripe:node-21-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 21.0.0: pins 2026-03-25.dahlia, drops Node 16, decimal_string fields become Stripe.Decimal, wrong webhook parsing method throws, effective 2026-03-25. Passed through during the bump. It pins 2026-03-25.dahlia and drops Node 16. decimal_string fields become Stripe.Decimal (unlikely here, since the code works with subscriptions and customers). Using the wrong webhook parsing method now throws; the code uses the standard constructEvent, so confirm the route still parses snapshot events.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "All `decimal_string` fields changed type from `string` to `Stripe.Decimal` in both request params and response objects."
- stripe:node-20-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 20.0.0: pins 2025-11-17.clover; v2 array params use indexed serialization (may break mock-server tests), effective 2025-11-18. Passed through during the bump. It pins 2025-11-17.clover. The indexed serialization of v2 array params only matters for mock-server tests; the repo makes no v2 calls.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "This may break any unit tests that expect the latter behavior when setting up a mock server."
- stripe:node-19-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 19.0.0: pins 2025-09-30.clover; parseThinEvent renamed parseEventNotification, v2 delete returns V2DeletedObject, v2 nullable props optional; 19.x deprecated (Files API timeout bug), effective 2025-09-30. Passed through during the bump. It pins 2025-09-30.clover. The parseThinEvent rename and the v2 delete and nullable changes don't touch the repo's v1 calls, but the API-version jump changes response types that the code compiles against. Skip the deprecated 19.x line.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Rename function `StripeClient.parseThinEvent` to `StripeClient.parseEventNotification` and remove the `Stripe.ThinEvent` interface."
- stripe:2026-09-30-endive-api-version (api-version): New API major 2026-09-30.endive carries breaking changes; pin it via Stripe-Version or upgrade SDKs (node 23, python 16, go v87), effective 2026-09-30. stripe-node 23 pins 2026-09-30.endive, so the SDK bump is the API-version move. None of the specific Endive breaking items match the repo's calls: no payment_method_types, billing_cycle_anchor, Financial Connections, Account Links v2, PayTo or Reserves.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md
  "As the first version in the Endive release, `2026-09-30.endive` introduces both breaking changes and new features."
- stripe:2026-03-25-dahlia-api-version (api-version): API major 2026-03-25.dahlia with breaking changes (Checkout ui_mode enum values, events_from on event destinations, Capabilities risk requirements, Stripe.js method removals), effective 2026-03-25. Dahlia sits between the repo's current SDK-pinned version and Endive, so its breaking changes ship with the same bump. Check that the webhook endpoint's API version in the Stripe dashboard matches the new SDK types.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia.md
  "As the first version in the Dahlia release, `2026-03-25.dahlia` introduces both breaking changes and new features"
- stripe:2026-03-25-checkout-ui-mode-enum (field-renamed): Checkout Session ui_mode enum values updated (Checkout Sessions and Payment Links), effective 2026-03-25. The repo calls checkout.sessions.create without ui_mode and later retrieves the session (app/verify-subscription/route.ts:14). The migration agent should check that no code reads or compares session.ui_mode against the old enum values after the version bump.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia.md
  "Updates Checkout Session UI mode enum values"
- stripe:runtime-go-1-24-drop (sdk-major): stripe-go will drop Go 1.24 in March 2027 major; Python 3.9 (stripe-python) March 2027; Node 20 (stripe-node) September 2027, effective 2027-03. The same notice says stripe-node drops Node 20 in the September 2027 major. While doing this upgrade, confirm the deploy runtime (Vercel/Next) is on Node 22 or later so the next major doesn't break.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/sdks/versioning.md
  "We’ll drop support for it in the September 2027 major release."

callSites.why: webhooks.constructEvent and the typed event payloads change across the SDK and API versions (stricter parsing in v21, reworked types in v22). The client construction in this file may need `new Stripe()`.

checkout.sessions.create params and response types change with the dahlia and endive pins. Confirm subscription_data, line_items and expires_at still type-check and behave the same; ui_mode is not passed.
The subscriptions.list response shape changed across the basil, clover, dahlia and endive versions; for example, period fields moved to subscription items in basil. Check which fields the code reads.
Reads subscription list results; subscription field locations changed across these API versions (for example current_period_end moved to items in 2025-03-31.basil).
checkout.sessions.retrieve response types change with the new pinned version; check the fields that are read.
This is a CommonJS script, which likely does `require('stripe')(key)`. That pattern breaks in v22 because Stripe must be constructed with `new`.
The subscriptions.list response shape changes with the API-version jump, and snapshot fields feed an rpc.
customers.retrieve can return a deleted customer, and the reworked types in v22 may change narrowing; the Stripe client construction here may also need `new`.
billingPortal.sessions.create; the client construction may need `new Stripe()` under v22.

## stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields [Verified]

### Change

Bumped stripe 15.12.0 -> 23.0.0 with npm. Client construction already used `new Stripe()` everywhere, and the repo does not use constructEventWithoutVerification. The only type break was `subscription.current_period_end`, which no longer exists. lib/billing-state.ts now reads `items.data[0].current_period_end`. I updated the billing test fixtures to put the period end on the item. Typecheck, build and all 150 tests pass.

Files touched:
- `lib/billing-state.ts`
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `tests/billing.test.cjs`

### Why

The SDK bump pulls in API versions from basil to endive. Since basil, the period end lives on subscription items, so the old subscription-level field no longer type-checks.

> Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| test | pass | pass | 0 |
| billing-period-end | pass | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- billing-period-end, added by the agent: `export NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL='http://127.0.0.1:54321' NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY='placeholder' SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY='placeholder' OPENAI_API_KEY='placeholder' BRAINTRUST_API_KEY='placeholder' WHOXY_API_KEY='placeholder' RAPID_API_KEY='placeholder' NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY='pk_test_placeholder' STRIPE_SECRET_KEY='sk_test_placeholder' STRIPE_ENDPOINT_SECRET='whsec_placeholder' STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID='price_placeholder_pro' STRIPE_BUSINESS_PRICE_ID='price_placeholder_business'; node --test tests/billing.test.cjs` (pass → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Prepared before the baseline:
- Checks ran with placeholder env: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, BRAINTRUST_API_KEY, WHOXY_API_KEY, RAPID_API_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_ENDPOINT_SECRET, STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID, STRIPE_BUSINESS_PRICE_ID.

Test of this change: `billing-period-end`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- The Stripe webhook endpoint's API version in the dashboard was not checked. It should match the endive pin or be confirmed compatible.
- The deploy runtime (Node 22 or later) was not checked.
- The SDK's runtime requirements were not checked against the deploy environment.
- No Stripe provider validators were run.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- The SDK now sends API version 2026-09-30.endive. The real response shapes from the live API are unverified.
- The period end is read from the first subscription item only. For a subscription with several items, this could differ from the old subscription-level value.

preparation.reasoning: No codegen or workspace builds are needed: the scripts are plain tsc, next build and node tests, and no install hooks are required. The build may load Supabase and Stripe clients at import time, so inert placeholder env vars from .env.example are provided, as the README suggests for compile-only builds.

review.summary: The diff covers the one source change the repo hits. It moves `current_period_end` from the subscription to `items.data[0]` in `lib/billing-state.ts`, which also covers `lib/billing.ts` and `scripts/reconcile-billing.cjs` because both call `billingSnapshot`. The removed items in the quoted changelog (`constructEventWithoutVerification`, the `ErrorType` export, `V2List` fields) are not used in the repo, and the webhook still calls `webhooks.constructEvent`. The bigger issue is scope. This jumps stripe-node from 15.12 to 23.0, and `stripeClient()` and the reconcile script never set `apiVersion`. Every live request will therefore move from the v15-pinned API version to `2026-09-30.endive`, across several Stripe API majors. Every check runs against hand-written mocks (`tests/billing.test.cjs`) or the type system. Typecheck passing is real evidence that the TS call sites still compile against v23 types. It does not prove the runtime behaviour of checkout, the billing portal, subscription listing or deletion checks against the new API version. 'Verified' overstates what the checks show; I'd treat this as needs-review until the live flows are exercised in test mode.

concerns.issue: `new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY!)` has no `apiVersion`, so the upgrade silently moves every request to `2026-09-30.endive`. That changes response shapes and semantics at every call site the match agent listed, not just `current_period_end`. Only the period-end move is handled, and none of it is exercised against real Stripe.

Entitlement now depends only on `items.data[0].current_period_end`. If that is missing (unexpected item shape, or a subscription with no items), `?? 0` makes the user free, which fails closed but would downgrade paying users if the field moved again. With multiple items the result depends on item order. That matches how `tier()` already reads the first item, so it is consistent, but it is worth confirming against the v23 `Stripe.SubscriptionItem` type.

This is an untyped CJS script that calls `require("stripe")` and `new Stripe(...)`. typecheck likely does not cover `.cjs` files and no test runs the script. I could not confirm that v23 still exposes the same CommonJS default export, so check the v23 package `exports`/main entry.

`constructEvent` is still used, but its signature and thrown-error behaviour under v23 are only checked by typecheck; the test mocks `constructEvent` entirely. Event payload shape follows the webhook endpoint's configured API version, not the SDK's. The handler only reads `data.object.customer` and refetches, which keeps this fairly safe. Still, confirm that `Invoice.customer` remains a top-level string or object in the endpoint's version.

Error handling matches `failure.type === "StripeInvalidRequestError"` and `param === "expires_at"`. Tests use fake error objects, so it is unproven that v23 still sets `type` to that string on thrown errors, especially now that the `ErrorType` export was removed. Check the v23 `StripeError` class.

checkFirst: Run checkout → webhook → `syncBilling` end to end in Stripe test mode on v23. Confirm `current_period_end` is populated on `items.data[0]` and that `plan_tier` is computed correctly.

Decide whether to pin `apiVersion` explicitly in `stripeClient()` and `scripts/reconcile-billing.cjs`, and review the Stripe API changelogs between the old pinned version and `2026-09-30.endive` for the endpoints used.
Verify that `require("stripe")` in `scripts/reconcile-billing.cjs` still returns a constructible class in v23.
Check that thrown `StripeInvalidRequestError` instances in v23 still expose `.type` and `.param` the way `app/checkout-session/route.ts` expects.
